title: fix(agents): keep tool-authored replies from hiding unfinished work
body:
Related: #164558

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes finished tool-authored replies hiding sibling failures, disappearing beside terminal tools, repeating pre-tool narration, or delivering content that result middleware withdrew.

## User Impact

Plugin tools can return a finished answer without a model restatement while unfinished or failed sibling work still receives a continuation. Only the originating input's preamble is replaced; earlier and later answers and errors remain visible. No configuration migration or automatic tool opt-in is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture and completion now share the finalized batch after result rewriting. Codex keeps candidates private until the upstream response closes and every model-emitted call has an eligible result; raw receipts cover late request registration and native siblings. Explicit terminal siblings retain their completion contract without dropping a finished reply. Canonical assistant identity keeps reused call IDs distinct and recovery idempotent.

Reply content comes only from `details.sourceReply`. Calls nested inside Code Mode return data to that program, never an implicit send. Codex's direct-reply fast path requires the model-only `direct-only` catalog. Existing message-tool delivery remains separate.

## Evidence

- Runtime verification executed at `3ace76ecaf4f082c7b00cba861513046b6ff65b6`. The final head adds only a documentation clarification learned from that live run; production and test source are unchanged. Documentation formatting and link audit pass (14,947 links, zero broken).
- Full `check:changed` on all 34 changed paths passed, including 27 core-test type shards, extension types, lint, and remaining guards. Full normal `pnpm build` passed in 5m26s. Its nonfatal UI-budget notice was 365.2 KiB startup JS versus 364.7 KiB; no UI source was changed.
- Real isolated Gateway, native Codex: **4/4 cases passed** with the actual Codex harness selected. Direct delivery was exact and once, with one raw model response and a terminal-release receipt. A real provider preamble was excluded from final delivery. Nested Code Mode did not auto-deliver its tool result. Both sibling calls were proven to belong to one raw response; the failing sibling caused a visible model continuation and no terminal release.
- Current embedded-runtime controls: **4/4 passed**. Agent-loop requests were 1 for direct/preamble and 2 for nested/sibling. Native evidence spans two authenticated, catalog-admitted model configurations; initial runs that did not exercise direct calls or same-response siblings remain fixture-inconclusive, not passes. No model allowlist or safety bypass was used.
- Red/green regressions cover finalized `message_end` rewriting, reused call IDs, response-only identity, terminal siblings, delayed native registration, and failure visibility. The refreshed 14-file selection passed in 216.56s. The final five-file selection passed 119 tests in 52.27s (`pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`); a mechanical owner extraction passed 48 related tests in 6.29s, and the corrected consumer fixture passed 13 in 44.44s. These selections overlap; per-test CI seconds are not measured.
- Independent review is clean through P2 after reproduced findings were fixed. Earlier local aggregates stopped on a line-count gate and then an outdated test fixture; both causes were corrected, and the full final aggregate passed. Earlier failed receipts were not relabeled successful.
- Source and built-artifact hashes stayed unchanged during every live run. All six attempted fixtures verified process/port shutdown and removed ephemeral state/config; artifact scans found zero raw credential matches. No operator Gateway changes or cloud allocations.
- Limits: no Telegram/Discord transport claim; native HTTP request counts are unmeasured (raw response receipts establish model continuations). Late extension mutation is integration-tested rather than claimed as live transport proof.
